summary: @qlik/oxlint-config preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package's preinstall lifecycle script (`node setup.mjs`) downloads the Bun runtime from the oven-sh/bun GitHub releases (v1.3.13) into a temporary directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` shipped in the tarball. `math_init.js` is a ~727 KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` compiled module with obfuscator.io-style string-array shuffling (a `WV8StW(...)` rotator over a large mixed numeric/string array `n7gIxM`) and hex-mangled identifiers; it is opaque and cannot be reviewed as source. The advertised purpose of the package is an oxlint configuration bundle, which has no need to fetch a second JavaScript runtime or execute compiled bytecode at install time. Fetching an alternate runtime specifically to run an obfuscated bundled payload outside Node's inspection surface is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern and grants the publisher arbitrary code execution on every installer at `npm install` time. Additionally, `package.json` declares `"files": ["src"]`, but the published tarball also contains root-level `setup.mjs` and the 727 KB `math_init.js` — the executable payload is not listed in the author-declared file manifest, consistent with tarball-smuggling under the `@qlik` scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
